ctx.x: Jack Lawrence wrote a string of pop hits in the forties, fifties, sixties, anyway, one of which he wrote for his friends John and Louise Eastman and their daughter Linda, who was about kindergarten age. This was 1946. He wrote a song for the kid. Oh, how does it go? Her name is Linda. “When I go to sleep/I never count sheep/I count all the charms about Linda. Lately it seems/in all my dreams/I dream with my arms about Linda. You’ve heard that song perhaps?
